cards.title: Iran says any Hormuz deal would bar military vessels
cards.summary: Iran says a proposed Oman-mediated shipping framework would keep military vessels out of the Strait of Hormuz while commercial traffic uses routes through Iranian and Omani waters.
detail: Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said Iran would not allow military vessels to transit the Strait of Hormuz under a potential agreement being discussed with Oman. The proposed framework would route commercial traffic through Iranian and Omani waters, according to the reported account.

The distinction matters because commercial passage and military access are separate operational questions. Hormuz remains a critical energy chokepoint, and a framework that protects merchant traffic but excludes warships would still leave enforcement, insurance, and naval-security questions unresolved.

The talks are not a confirmed reopening. The next evidence is a formal agreement, operating rules, and proof that commercial traffic resumes; the current card treats the arrangement as a proposal and keeps the wider regional consequences uncertain.
cards.why: The proposed shipping rules are the clearest current test of whether Hormuz diplomacy can become an operating arrangement.
verifiedFacts: AP reported Iran’s proposed exclusion of military vessels from a potential Hormuz framework.
The reported commercial route would use Iranian and Omani waters.
attributedClaims: Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi described the proposal on state television.
analysis: A commercial-only framework could reduce some supply risk without resolving military access or enforcement.
uncertainty: No signed agreement, reopening date, or enforcement mechanism was verified by the 07:00 cutoff.

cards.title: Federal judge blocks Ohio motor-voter proof-of-citizenship rule
cards.summary: A federal judge temporarily blocked Ohio from requiring documentary citizenship proof before offering voter registration at motor-vehicle offices; the state says it will appeal.
detail: U.S. District Judge Solomon Oliver Jr. temporarily blocked Ohio from requiring documentary proof of citizenship when eligible residents register through the Bureau of Motor Vehicles. The order also addresses the state process for offering registration to driver-license applicants.

The ruling applies ahead of the Oct. 5 registration deadline for the fall midterms and turns a state registration procedure into a direct federal-law test. The court found the challenged process likely conflicts with the National Voter Registration Act; Ohio Secretary of State Frank LaRose said the state would appeal.

The immediate practical question is how the BMV implements the injunction while the case proceeds. The ruling is a preliminary court action, not a final resolution of every Ohio election-document rule, so implementation and appellate steps remain open.
cards.why: It changes the registration process for Ohio residents and has an immediate midterm-election deadline.

The official report lists New England Revolution as Columbus’s next opponent on Aug. 30 at 4:30 p.m. ET. The elimination is settled; the recovery question is how the Crew handles the return to league play after a two-goal first-half deficit.

cards.title: Oil slips as Hormuz talks temper supply fears
cards.summary: Brent and U.S. crude eased after a volatile session as traders weighed Iran–Oman shipping talks against the risk that the strait remains constrained.

The market is pricing two competing signals: a possible route framework that could reduce supply disruption, and the absence of a confirmed reopening arrangement. That makes the move a risk-premium adjustment rather than evidence that shipping constraints have ended.
The next update depends on formal shipping rules, enforcement, and actual tanker movement. This card describes market conditions only and does not recommend a position.
